title: Law of conservation of mass
competency: State the law of conservation of mass.

keywords.def: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

en.text: The law of conservation of mass says matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. The mass of the reactants equals the mass of the products. Burning paper seems to lose mass only because gases escape into the air.

screens.title: Lighter ash
screens.ask: Paper burns. The ash is lighter than the paper. Was mass destroyed?
opts: No, gases escaped into the air
screens.after:
Burning makes carbon dioxide and water vapour. These gases float away.
If you caught them, the total mass would be the same.
Mass was not destroyed.
screens.best: No, gases escaped into the air

screens.title: 3.3.3 Law of conservation of mass
paras: Matter is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction.
The mass of the reactants is exactly equal to the mass of the products.

screens.title: Burn magnesium in a closed bottle
screens.ask: Choose how much magnesium burns. Compare the mass before and after.
screens.note: 24 g of magnesium uses 16 g of oxygen. Before and after are always equal: mass is conserved.

screens.title: Why does burnt paper seem lighter?
steps: Paper burns with oxygen from the air.
Products: ash, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
In open air the gases float away. The scale shows only the ash.
So the ash seems lighter than the paper.
In a closed jar the gases stay in.
Then the mass before and after is the same.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

screens.text: State the law: what does the law of conservation of mass say?
opts: Mass is lost when things burn
Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction
screens.ans: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction
screens.why:
The law says matter is neither created nor destroyed.
So the mass of reactants equals the mass of products.
Burning only seems to lose mass, when gases escape.
Products are not always heavier.

screens.text: True or false: in a chemical reaction atoms are neither created nor destroyed.
screens.why:
Atoms only rearrange in a reaction.
No atom is made. No atom is lost.
This is the law of conservation of mass.
So the statement is true.

screens.ask: Use the law: 10 g of reactants react completely. The products have a mass of ___ g.
screens.why:
Mass of reactants = mass of products.
The reactants are 10 g.
So the products are 10 g.
screens.clue: Mass is not lost or gained.

screens.ask: Use the law: in a closed bottle, 24 g of magnesium burns with 16 g of oxygen. The magnesium oxide has a mass of ___ g.
screens.why:
The bottle is closed, so nothing escapes.
Mass of reactants: 24 g + 16 g = 40 g.
Mass is conserved.
So the magnesium oxide has a mass of 40 g.
screens.clue: Add the masses of the reactants.

test.text: True or false: matter is created in a chemical reaction.
test.why:
The law of conservation of mass says matter is neither created nor destroyed.
Atoms only rearrange.
So matter is not created: False.

test.text: Complete the law: the mass of reactants ___ the mass of products.
test.why:
Matter is neither created nor destroyed.
So no mass is gained or lost.
Mass of reactants is equal to mass of products.

test.text: Conservation of mass: burnt paper ash is lighter than the paper because
test.why:
Paper + oxygen → ash + carbon dioxide + water vapour.
The gases escape into the air.
The scale weighs only the ash.
Mass was not destroyed: gases escaped.

test.ask: Use the law: 5 g of A reacts with 3 g of B. The products weigh ___ g.
test.why:
Mass of reactants = 5 g + 3 g = 8 g.
Mass is conserved.
So the products weigh 8 g.

test.ask: Find the missing mass: a reaction makes 18 g of water from 2 g of hydrogen and ___ g of oxygen.
test.why:
Mass of products = mass of reactants.
18 g = 2 g + oxygen.
Oxygen = 18 − 2 = 16 g.
Check: 2 + 16 = 18.
